grid.title: Photoelectric effect: Planck's constant with {metal}
grid.unknown: Planck's constant, and the work function of {metal}

metal.label: a caesium cathode
metal.note: Caesium has the smallest work function of all the metals, so even the green 546 nm mercury line still frees electrons from it.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Electron work function of the elements': caesium 2.14 eV (polycrystalline)

metal.label: a rubidium cathode
metal.note: Rubidium sits just above caesium in the same group and in the same table: a slightly larger work function, so the whole line of stopping potentials drops a little.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Electron work function of the elements': rubidium 2.26 eV (polycrystalline)

metal.label: a potassium cathode
metal.note: With potassium the green 546 nm line is already below the threshold and gives no current at all, which is a result in itself.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Electron work function of the elements': potassium 2.30 eV (polycrystalline)

metal.label: a sodium cathode
metal.note: Sodium's threshold wavelength is about 525 nm, so only the three shorter mercury lines work here.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Electron work function of the elements': sodium 2.36 eV (polycrystalline)

metal.label: a barium cathode
metal.note: Barium needs more energy again: the stopping potentials are small, so the 0.01 V least count matters much more here.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Electron work function of the elements': barium 2.52 eV (polycrystalline)
